subject: Evaluation runway: proposed MAP edits and containment plan
messages:
From: Acme Ops <ops@acme.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot evaluation: data/latency observations and potential acceptance slip

Hi Mina / Ben,

Quick heads up from our side after the last two test runs: token throughput is consistently ~18% below the MAP projection once we hit parallel ingestion >8 streams. Latency spikes occur during long-prefix runs (seen at ~2.1s p90). Procurement is nervous about the go-live window if these continue.

Can we get an updated MAP that reflects realistic throughput & a short mitigation plan? Procurement asked whether a 2-week window shift would be required to accommodate additional tests.

Attachments: run-logs-0821.csv (we've uploaded to your shared folder)

Thanks,
Lara
Acme Ops

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Acme Ops <ops@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot evaluation: data/latency observations and potential acceptance slip

Lara — thanks for the data and callout. We've reviewed the logs and agree the current MAP assumptions are optimistic for the long-prefix ingestion pattern.

Proposed immediate steps (short list):
- Short-term: deploy a revised batch/kv-cache profile to the evaluation cluster tonight (non-disruptive) and rerun two long-prefix tests tomorrow morning.
- MAP edit: adjust acceptance window by +10 working days and add a gated smoke test after the reruns before we move to full-scale runs.
- Containment: if reruns still show >12% degradation, we trigger the fallback model (quantized variant) for the customer acceptance window.

I'm attaching a compact MAP delta (acme-map-v2.xlsx) and a one-page risk heatmap.

Can we get a procurement contact for formal sign-off if we need the 10-day adjustment? If Acme prefers a 2-week shift we'll surface the downstream impact on deployment cadence and SLAs.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

---Attachment: acme-map-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
---Attachment: close-runway-risk-heatmap.png (image stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot evaluation: data/latency observations and potential acceptance slip

Marissa — forwarding for visibility. Acme's ops flagged a throughput/latency variance that pushes acceptance risk. Mina's recommended an operational MAP delta (10 working days) + fallback path.

Key ask: are we comfortable offering a one-time 10-day acceptance window shift (no invoice change) vs. holding the original date and triggering the fallback model (which may reduce measured quality by small margin)? Procurement will need a formal note to approve the MAP delta.

If we approve the 10-day shift, I recommend offering a limited performance credit tied to the acceptance metric (e.g., 5% credit if p95 > target after final reruns) to keep goodwill.

Can you weigh in before EOD? Quick background: ACME-2025-042 is mid-size strategic; delaying will compress our Q3 delivery cadence slightly but reduces escalation risk.

—Ben

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Acme Ops <ops@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Aug 2025 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed MAP revision and acceptance cadence (ACME-2025-042) — request for formal sign-off

Team — per our review and internal escalation, please find the proposed changes to the MAP and acceptance cadence attached. Summary below: 

1) Acceptance window: shift by +10 business days from the current target (new target: 2025-09-12).
2) Gate conditions: two validated long-prefix stress runs (baseline + post-config changes) with p95 latency <= 2.0s and throughput within -8% of MAP projection.
3) Fallback: if gating fails, we will switch to the quantized compatible model for acceptance runs and continue optimization in parallel.
4) Commercial: if we move the window, Redwood will offer a one-time 5% invoice credit tied to measured p95 deviation beyond the gate (details in revised-sow.docx).

Attachments: revised-sow.docx (SOW excerpt), acme-map-v2.xlsx, close-runway-risk-heatmap.png

Please reply with a single-line sign-off ("ACCEPT - 10BD shift") or request a short call. Procurement approval will be sufficient to update the MAP and the schedule.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Enterprise AE
Redwood Inference

---Attachment: revised-sow.docx (doc stub)

From: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Ops <ops@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Aug 2025 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP revision and acceptance cadence (ACME-2025-042) — request for formal sign-off

Mina — ACCEPT - 10BD shift. Procurement approves the revised acceptance window and the commercial credit as outlined.

We'll record this in our purchase tracker and notify legal for the minor SOW amendment. Thanks for laying out the fallback; ops will coordinate the reruns tomorrow.

Regards,
Sonia Patel
Head of Procurement, Acme Corp
